title: the-decompose-door-accepts-a-commons-output
intention: The decompose door's writes_to check accepts an address inside CairnCommons as well as inside the cairn repo, so a concept-piece's chart (its only output a .md in the commons) can berth.
why: No concept-piece can be charted today: write_decompose refuses a writes_to outside the cairn repo, and a concept-piece's only output is a .md in CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code, so its BUILDME entry lane a_berthed_chart_chain_claims_the_ticket never opens. Measured 2026-10-04: df05d93da4c0's chart refused at decompose ('is outside the cairn repo'). The rule's why (68f1fc073512: a write this system does not gate and git cannot see) is false for the commons, and Akien answered open-90d38cb2bdca 'a agreed'.
traces_to: Akien's answer to CairnCommons/questions/open-90d38cb2bdca.json ('a agreed'); Law 6; Law 9; RULE 1 (inside codemother's decompose machine; the promotion judge it composes is sibling fb85042b8342)
how: cairn/devices/codemother/machines/decompose/decompose.py writes_to_lacks: an entry is in bounds when its normalized path lies under root or under os.path.join(os.path.dirname(root), 'CairnCommons'). Anything else still lacks, with a sentence naming both roots. A new proof beside the machine.
falsifier: GREEN when (1) writes_to_lacks over a piece whose writes_to is an absolute path under the commons root returns []; (2) /etc/passwd and a path under ~/.cairn each return one lack containing 'outside'; (3) that lack names both the cairn repo and CairnCommons. RED if any fails or test_chart_decompose reds. Horizon: this ticket PROVED and df05d93da4c0's chart berthed.
watchme: none, because df05d93da4c0's chart berthing (CairnCommons/tickets/df05d93da4c0-an-unvouched-green-completes-and-notifies.json) is the first use and is measured at its BUILDME
children: none, because the change is one function and one proof inside the decompose machine

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: in cairn/devices/codemother/machines/decompose/decompose.py writes_to_lacks, before the loop add `commons = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(root), "CairnCommons")`; the in-bounds test becomes `any(resolved == r or resolved.startswith(r + os.sep) for r in (root, commons))` with `resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(root, addr))` unchanged. The lack text becomes "%s: `writes_to` %s is outside the cairn repo and CairnCommons — a piece may only declare output this system gates writes to" (still containing 'outside the cairn repo', so test_chart_decompose.py:279 and :285 stay true). The docstring's 'IN-REPO' sentence names both roots and cites this ticket and Akien's answer to open-90d38cb2bdca.

D2: SETTLED: new proof cairn/devices/codemother/machines/decompose/proofs/test_the_decompose_door_accepts_a_commons_output.py, the same shape as cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_over_a_red_under_other_conditions_notifies.py (docstring, _REPO_ROOT = parents[6] (measured: the first ancestor holding .git; [5] is the cairn package dir), sys.path insert, PROVES dict, main() printing GREEN/RED, exit 1 on any fail). Each tooth imports `from cairn.devices.codemother.machines.decompose.decompose import writes_to_lacks` and `from cairn.tools.chain.grammar import CAIRN_ROOT` inside its body. Teeth: '1' test_a_commons_address_lacks_nothing: `writes_to_lacks([{"what": "p", "writes_to": [os.path.join(os.path.dirname(CAIRN_ROOT), "CairnCommons", "intentions-not-beside-code", "I-x.md")]}]) == []`. '2' test_an_address_outside_both_roots_still_lacks: for each of "/etc/passwd" and str(Path.home() / ".cairn" / "x.json"), the call returns exactly one lack containing 'outside'. '3' test_the_lack_names_both_roots: the /etc/passwd lack contains 'cairn repo' and 'CairnCommons'. Validation berths beside it through the tester seal.

D3: SETTLED: why widening the root is a fix and not a weakening: the check exists to refuse a declared output this system does not gate and git cannot see (68f1fc073512); CLAUDE.md berths every concept-piece in CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/, so a root of the cairn repo alone contradicts the design it guards and leaves no concept-piece chartable; CairnCommons is git-tracked and every record write in it passes the artifact door, so it meets the rule's own why exactly as the cairn repo does, while /etc/passwd and instance-space ~/.cairn still fail it and still red.
decisions.step: unlisted: why the second root is sound

decisions.text: D1 structure, measured 2026-10-04 at decompose.py:152-172: writes_to_lacks sets `lacks = []`, returns early on is_skeleton, then runs `for i, sp in enumerate(sub_problems):` with an inner `for addr in addrs:`; inside the inner loop, after the non-string check, line 169 is `resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(root, addr))` and lines 170-172 are `if not (resolved == root or resolved.startswith(root + os.sep)): lacks.append(...)`. Insert `commons = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(root), "CairnCommons")` on the line right after `lacks = []`; leave line 169 as is; replace the test on line 170 with `if not any(resolved == r or resolved.startswith(r + os.sep) for r in (root, commons)):`; change only the appended sentence to "%s: `writes_to` %s is outside the cairn repo and CairnCommons — a piece may only declare output this system gates writes to" % (where, addr).

D2 template, inline: docstring; `from __future__ import annotations`; `import os`, `import sys`, `from pathlib import Path`; `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[6]`; `sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT))`; `PROVES = {"9bd674040f48": {"1": "test_a_commons_address_lacks_nothing", "2": "test_an_address_outside_both_roots_still_lacks", "3": "test_the_lack_names_both_roots"}}`; helper `_lacks(addr)` importing writes_to_lacks inside its body and returning `writes_to_lacks([{"what": "p", "writes_to": [addr]}])`; CAIRN_ROOT is the module-level constant at cairn/tools/chain/grammar.py:65, imported inside tooth 1 as `from cairn.tools.chain.grammar import CAIRN_ROOT`; main() loops over the PROVES values with try/except Exception, prints "  ok   <name>" or "  FAIL <name>: <type>: <exc>", then RED or GREEN, returns 1 on any fail; `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`.
